context: Initial scaffold with members=[] and no Cargo.lock failed all 6 required checks. Fix: bitty-ai-core placeholder crate plus committed Cargo.lock. Lesson: never push a Rust workspace without at least one member and lockfile.
title: Empty workspace breaks all locked CI jobs

consequences: Direct merges without closeout will trip the gate; fix is publish + rerun, as done here (e2df253, rerun success).
context: 2026-09-14: bitty-ai#14 merged directly to main (edee2ad) without snapshot closeout; Snapshot-source gate failed with snapshot at 13f0306 behind main.
decision_body: Every merge to main MUST be followed immediately by just workflow-publish from updated main plus a snapshot-source green check before the owning task is completed. Whoever merges owns this step.
rationale: The gate compares snapshot source against main HEAD; any main advance without a fresh snapshot trips it. Publishing first, then verifying, keeps main green.
title: Snapshot must be published before merge closeout completes

consequences: The real gate still passes today with the loud BOOTSTRAP PASS line instead of a silent 0 binding-path pass, so the bootstrap tree stays compatible and the exception is visible in any diff. The cost is a deliberate source edit when the first binding crate lands. The authority conflict is NOT resolved in bitty-ai-docs and needs a commander decision: either the design's migration text gains an explicit bootstrap clause, or the design keeps expecting zero binding crates and the constant stays. No binding crate exists yet, so classes 1-4 are dormant in production and enforced only by the regression suite.
context: The AI-0145 gate returned 0 for BINDING_PATHS=(), which contradicts the fail-closed criterion the task required. The design authority (bitty-ai-docs/architecture/host-boundary-trait-design.md, Migration plan step 1) expects the gate to land on a tree with zero binding crates, so the authority and the acceptance criterion genuinely conflict. Changing the design document is a separate repository and is not authorized in AI-0152, so the conflict is recorded here instead.
decision_body: Default to fail-closed: an empty BINDING_PATHS set is a configuration error (exit 1). The single exception is the reviewed source constant BINDING_SET_BOOTSTRAP=1, which must be validated to be 0 or 1 unconditionally and prints an explicit BOOTSTRAP PASS line naming the exception. It is a source constant, not an environment variable, because an environment switch would make the fail-closed state opt-out-able at run time and therefore not fail-closed. It is removed in the same change that declares the first binding crate. Documented in the gate header (scripts/host-boundary-lint.sh:26-34), enforced at :741-745, covered by suite cases 47-48, and described in CONTRIBUTING.md.
title: Empty binding set fails closed; reviewed bootstrap source constant is the single exception

consequences: The gate is now honest about what it proves, documented in CONTRIBUTING.md with an explicit pass-does-not-prove section. The commander must decide whether to accept the trait as the real enforcement and treat the gate as defence in depth, and must sync bitty-ai-docs: the design's Lint-gate rule specification lists four concrete rg patterns and does not mention the bare-identifier rule, the source-closure validation, the path-dependency classification, the construct-specific allowlist, or the bootstrap exception. Those are implementation-level strengthenings consistent with the section's stated intent (any direct reference to a Core-owned item outside the Core crate fails the build), but the canonical text should say so. Not done here: bitty-ai-docs is a separate repository and out of scope.
context: AI-0145 has now failed two review rounds against compiling bypasses. Round 1 (13f5861) missed 18-21 spellings; round 2 (0446724, PX-0593) found five blocking classes, all demonstrated with compiling fixtures. Two independent reviewers have shown that enumerating textual spellings is an unwinnable game: each fix closed the reported case and left the neighbouring spelling open. This is inherent to a text-based check, not a defect of one implementation.
decision_body: Implement the narrowest sound thing the textual approach can carry, and state the limit plainly. What is now sound: every file the compiler can read for a binding crate is inside the scanned set (Cargo target sources validated, textual source inclusions validated, symlinks rejected, in-repository path dependencies classified), and within that set the Core crate identifier is banned everywhere, so no local spelling or macro route reaches Core. What is not sound and cannot be: text is not semantics. Three residuals stay accepted and documented (external proc-macro expansion, generated/build-script/OUT_DIR source, comment and string false positives), plus one review-visible case (a crate listed in NON_BINDING_PATHS may re-export Core) and one obfuscation limit (an identifier assembled at run time from fragments). The alternative is proposed as a separate written proposal for the commander, NOT taken here: keep the textual gate as a cheap ratchet and promote the design's HostBoundary trait as the only mechanism that can actually be sound, because a trait bound is checked by the compiler on every call site rather than by pattern enumeration. AI-0152 does not introduce the trait, does not migrate call sites, and does not close AIQ-31.
title: The textual host-boundary gate is a ratchet, not a soundness proof; promotion to a typed mechanism is proposed, not taken
